name: What's the difference between a workers' comp claim and a personal injury lawsuit?

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between a workers' comp claim and a personal injury lawsuit?

acceptedAnswer.text: Workers' compensation is a no-fault insurance system designed to provide benefits for work-related injuries, regardless of who was at fault. It covers medical expenses and lost wages, but generally prevents you from suing your employer for pain and suffering. A personal injury lawsuit, conversely, requires proving negligence by another party to recover damages, which can include medical costs, lost wages, pain and suffering. You might pursue a personal injury claim if a third party, not your employer, was responsible for your workplace injury.
acceptedAnswer.description: Workers' comp is a no-fault system for work injuries, while personal injury lawsuits require proving negligence. Workers' comp typically covers medical costs and lost wages, not pain and suffering.
